attack_focus: repeated/distinct generator-matrix columns in trellis complexity
exact endpoint-product dynamic programs under alternative terminology

new_findings.detail: For 1-dimensional classes, repeated identical subspaces are parallel matroid elements. A repeated geometric class of multiplicity at least two has exactly the prefix-status progression RIGHT_ONLY -> BOTH -> LEFT_ONLY. Additional middle copies do not create a new span state.
new_findings.novelty_consequence: Do not make historical-priority claims for the bare middle-copy deletion / first-last sufficiency lemma unless an expert specifically confirms it is not standard folklore.

new_findings.detail: Targeted searches for matroid pathwidth / trellis-width parameterized by number of parallel classes, distinct columns, repeated columns, clone classes, or distinct represented geometric classes did not return an exact endpoint-state algorithm or equivalent 2-state/3-state class product graph.

Cong-Xu-Zhao (arXiv:2608.16298) use the number of parallel classes in bounded-rank contraction minors for deterministic minimum-cocircuit algorithms. This proves that 'parameterize a matroid algorithm by parallel classes' is not itself novel.
new_findings.consequence: A3 novelty must remain tied to the exact pathwidth endpoint quotient and DP, not the generic parameter choice.

new_findings.detail: Choi-Korhonen-Oum (arXiv:2605.14428) give faster algorithms for branch-width and path-width of represented matroids over fixed finite fields; the inspected abstract/corollary framing is parameterized by width and field, not by the number of distinct geometric/parallel classes, and does not state the A3 endpoint product graph.

Modern matroid/pathwidth work explicitly treats pathwidth as a linear-layout parameter of a symmetric submodular connectivity function. Current targeted searches did not locate a general duplicate-element/twin-element endpoint theorem that directly yields the A3 2^s*3^r state graph.

component_A_middle_copy_invariance.description: Multiplicity >=2 contributes only first/last endpoint events; extra copies do not change span status.
component_A_middle_copy_invariance.reason: Elementary from idempotent span/connectivity semantics and plausible folklore under parallel-extension language.

component_B_exact_endpoint_quotient.description: Singleton classes contribute two states; repeated classes contribute three states, yielding the exact product state space 2^s*3^r.

component_D_algorithmic_parameterization.description: O(k*3^k) combinatorial bottleneck DP after 2^k subset-rank preprocessing, where k is the number of distinct geometric subspaces.
component_D_algorithmic_parameterization.note: This is currently the strongest novelty-bearing part of A3.

closest_public_results_checked_in_v3.relationship: General constructive FPT pathwidth for finite-field subspace arrangements using trajectory/full-set machinery; no inspected statement of distinct-class endpoint quotient.

Uses bounded number of parallel classes as a parameter in a different matroid algorithmic problem; kills novelty of the generic parameterization pattern, not the A3 pathwidth DP.

strongest_current_candidate_claim: For finite-field subspace-arrangement pathwidth, the A3 package gives an exact quotient of layouts by class endpoint status, with singleton/repeated class alphabets of size 2/3, exact state and transition counts, and an O(k*3^k) bottleneck DP parameterized by the number k of distinct geometric subspaces after subset-rank preprocessing. No exact or directly subsuming predecessor has been located in the current targeted search.
reviewer_killer_questions_v3: Is pathwidth invariant under adding a third or later parallel copy to an existing parallel class a standard named/recorded lemma? Please cite the earliest source.
Has matroid pathwidth or code trellis-width been parameterized by the number of parallel classes / distinct generator-matrix columns, even if the algorithm is not described as endpoint compression?
Is there a standard quotient of linear layouts of parallel/clone classes into states {not-started, open, closed} or an equivalent interval/event representation?
Does any theorem for symmetric submodular connectivity functions with duplicate/twin ground elements imply the entire 2^s*3^r state graph, not merely the middle-copy lemma?
Does a coding-theory span-form / trellis construction already use only the first and last positions of repeated identical generator columns to optimize trellis-width globally?
